- **Save, then reopen:** save, discard and the next `loadDraft` are ordered by the queue. `closed` blocks the timer, AppState and unmount writes after `addEntry`. The old draft does not reappear.
- **Edit save:** state is reset to `saved` (media URIs under `media/`) before the draft folder is deleted, so previews are not broken. `storedSignature` equals `sig(entrySnapshot(saved))`, and the post-reset snapshot matches it: trimmed text, location on/place, tag ids and attachments' uri/name all line up. No rewrite follows.
- **Cancel edit:** resets to the entry, then `keep=false` and the draft is discarded, unless bug 1 applies.
- **Clear all content:** `canSaveDraft` false leads to discard. A discard never deletes files that state still references, because discard means there are no media refs or only `media/` refs.
- **Deleting:** `removeEntry` discards before notifying. `clearAll` and import call `discardAllDrafts`.
- **Copies:** each file is copied once per session (the `copies` map plus an exists check). Prune is serialized and only deletes files not referenced by the snapshot just written. A failed copy deletes the partial target (Android `copyFileNio` can leave one) and returns null, so text is still written. `storedSignature` is reset on failure, so the next change retries.
- **React effects:** `persistDraft` is stable (`[]` deps, reads `latest`), so there are no stale closures and no render loops. A StrictMode double mount is a no-op because the signature equals `initialSignature`. A view-mode screen never writes when `existing` changes elsewhere, because the snapshot signature does not change.
- **expo-file-system 57:** `File(Paths.document, "media/x.jpg")` joins correctly through the URL pathname. `Directory.uri` always ends in "/" and `File.uri` never does, on both iOS and Android, so the `documentPrefix` slicing matches `mediaFileUri` output. `copy` is async and leaves the source intact. `moveSync({overwrite:true})` deletes then renames, which is not atomic, but a crash in between leaves only the pending file, which `loadDraft` reads. `write` creates or truncates. `Directory.delete` is recursive on Android and uses `removeItem` on iOS. `list()` is used by name only, so `/private/var` forms don't matter.
- **iOS container path change:** handled, because refs are relative and resolved against the current `Paths.document`. Percent-encoding can't double-encode, because `%` is excluded by the ref regex.
- **Recorder and image-manipulator URIs** are unique per take or render (UUID names), so keying copies by source URI is safe.
- **Backup:** export ignores drafts. Import discards them after `pruneReplacedMedia`, which also drops any unsaved "new" draft; that is a product choice, not a bug.

content.text:
I fixed the real problems the two reviewers found. Tests (31), typecheck and Biome all pass. Nothing is committed or pushed, and none of it has been run on a device or emulator yet.

**Problems that could still cost you a draft, now fixed:**
- **A failed save was never retried.** If a write failed, the same content was never written again. Now it retries on the next change or the next time you leave.
- **One missing file lost the whole draft.** If a photo was already cleared from the cache, the text was lost too. Now only that one item is dropped.
- **Leaving quickly could lose the last keystrokes.** If you pressed back and reopened a new entry while the screen was still animating out, the new screen could load the older autosave. Now it saves when back is pressed, before the animation starts.
- **A crash during a write could restore the older version.** Now the newer copy is read first if it's complete.

**Smaller glitches, now fixed:**
- A leftover draft that was empty, or identical to the entry, could force the entry into edit mode every time and never get cleared. It's now ignored and cleaned up on the next autosave.
- All drafts shared one queue, so copying a large file for one draft made every other entry wait to open. Each draft now has its own queue; "Delete all" still waits for all of them.
- After saving a new entry, its draft files were deleted while the closing screen could still be showing their previews. They're now cleared after you're taken back.
- Importing a backup now clears drafts, so an old edit can't overwrite the imported entry.

**Code cleanup:**
- Draft files reuse the existing media filename and extension helpers instead of a copy of them.
- The "is this draft worth keeping" rule now lives in one function in `DraftTransform.ts`, shared by the autosave and the screen.
- `reset` always takes an explicit target, and a stale comment is gone.
- I didn't add any test files; the one from before covers the draft format and path checks.

**Known limits, left as they are:**
- **A recording still in progress** when you leave or the app dies is not saved. Finished recordings are. Fixing that means stopping the recorder when you leave, which changes how recording behaves.
- **Typing during the moment an edit is saving** is replaced by the saved version. Keeping it would have meant a hidden draft behind the view screen.
- **Backup files with spaces or unusual characters in their names** get copied into the draft while you edit. The result is still correct; it just copies more than it needs to. Files the app creates don't hit this.
- **Leaving the app during a very large file copy:** the text is written only after the copy finishes, so it can be lost if the app dies mid-copy. The half-second autosave has usually copied the file already.

Still needs a device check: swiping the app away from recents, a forced crash, Android clearing its cache, and restoring after an iOS update.

git add -A src scripts && git status --short && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Keep compose drafts across back, backgrounding, and crashes

Unsaved compose content lived only in React state and picked media pointed
into the OS cache, so leaving the screen, swiping the app away, or a crash
lost the draft.

Drafts for new entries and for edits now autosave under
documents/drafts/<key>/ with their own copies of cache-backed files. They
are written after a short pause, when the app leaves the foreground, and
before the screen is removed, and are restored when the same entry is
composed again. A draft is discarded only after its entry commits, or when
it is emptied, cancelled, its entry is deleted, or the timeline is
replaced by an import.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -1 && git status --short
